(a) Short Title.—This Act may be cited as the “Katrina Emergency Tax Relief Act of 2005”. 
    (b) Table of Contents.—The table of contents for this Act is as follows:

Sec. 1. 
Short title, etc.

Sec. 2. 
Hurricane Katrina disaster area.

TITLE I—
SPECIAL RULES FOR USE OF RETIREMENT FUNDS FOR RELIEF RELATING TO HURRICANE KATRINA

Sec. 101. 
Tax-favored withdrawals from retirement plans for relief relating to Hurricane Katrina.

Sec. 102. 
Recontributions of withdrawals for home purchases cancelled due to Hurricane Katrina.

Sec. 103. 
Loans from qualified plans for relief relating to Hurricane Katrina.

Sec. 104. 
Provisions relating to plan amendments.

TITLE II—
EMPLOYMENT RELIEF

Sec. 201. 
Work opportunity tax credit for Hurricane Katrina employees.

Sec. 202. 
Employee retention credit for employers affected by Hurricane Katrina.

TITLE III—
CHARITABLE GIVING INCENTIVES

Sec. 301. 
Temporary suspension of limitations on charitable contributions.

Sec. 302. 
Additional exemption for housing Hurricane Katrina displaced individuals.

Sec. 303. 
Increase in standard mileage rate for charitable use of vehicles.

Sec. 304. 
Mileage reimbursements to charitable volunteers excluded from gross income.

Sec. 305. 
Charitable deduction for contributions of food inventory.

Sec. 306. 
Charitable deduction for contributions of book inventories to public schools.

TITLE IV—
ADDITIONAL TAX RELIEF PROVISIONS

Sec. 401. 
Exclusions of certain cancellations of indebtedness by reason of Hurricane Katrina.

Sec. 402. 
Suspension of certain limitations on personal casualty losses.

Sec. 403. 
Required exercise of authority under section 7508A for tax relief relating to Hurricane Katrina.

Sec. 404. 
Special rules for mortgage revenue bonds.

Sec. 405. 
Extension of replacement period for nonrecognition of gain for property located in Hurricane Katrina disaster area.

Sec. 406. 
Special rule for determining earned income.

Sec. 407. 
Secretarial authority to make adjustments regarding taxpayer and dependency status.

TITLE V—
EMERGENCY REQUIREMENT

Sec. 501. 
Emergency requirement.

fable.w: This section contains only the short title and a table of contents for a tax relief act. The tempting reading is that headings such as "Secretarial authority to make adjustments" or the references to charitable volunteers imply rulemaking or outside involvement, but these are bare section titles with no operative text. Nothing here establishes a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or a right to sue.

qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Act provides relief to individuals (taxpayers, employers, charities), it involves "participation" by the public. However, the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and this section is merely a table of contents listing statutory provisions. It does not describe any process where the government consults with or coordinates with outside parties before making a decision. The text is purely structural and definitional.

opus.w: This section only gives the Act's short title and lists the headings of its sections. It does not set up any process for people outside the federal government to take part in a federal decision. Headings that mention Secretarial authority or charitable volunteers name the topics of other sections. They do not create comment periods, consultation, hearings, advisory bodies or a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section provided is a table of contents and short title for the Katrina Emergency Tax Relief Act of 2005. It lists various tax provisions but does not contain any language requiring or recommending consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) in the decision-making process. The definition of participation requires interaction with outside parties before a decision is made, such as through advisory committees or public hearings, none of which are present in this text.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Act provides tax relief to individuals and businesses, it involves "participation" in the sense that these outside parties benefit from the government's decision. However, the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and merely receiving a benefit or having a tax code change applied to one is not "participation" in the decision-making process (e.g., consultation, advisory boards, public hearings). The text provided is merely a table of contents and short title; it contains no procedural requirements for outside parties to consult with the government, comment on rules, or serve on advisory bodies.
